description: BLIND-SPOT CLOSURE R9 (proposition-grain belief content, 2026-07-12). domains/character_tom.py's `_nested_entity`/`_ground_attitude_complement` mechanically stamp the reader's OWN complement-clause parse (the full [rel, a0, a1] predication, plus its verbatim span) onto every Level-2 belief/goal node (`SmEntity{nested:1}` for belief/knowledge, `SmEvent{verb:'want'}` for desire) as `proposition`/`proposition_span` -- unconditionally, the SAME mechanical mint discipline `situation_model_reader.ingest_predication` already uses for every other node attr. This ONE rule is the DECISION surface: a Level-2 node carrying a `proposition_span` (and not yet marked) is ELIGIBLE for full-proposition rendering, marked via `proposition_capture=1`. `reflective_faculty._run_interlocutor_model` reads `proposition_capture` before preferring `proposition_span` over the old head-grain `referent`/`idx_intentionality` -- so ablating this rule (remove_rule) reverts every render to the pre-closure head-grain text ('believing new_scheduler') even though the richer data is still sitting on the node, proving the closure's DECISION genuinely lives in the rule, not in the mechanical mint. Matched via a fresh `is_attitude_level2` self-edge (the SAME single-node self-match idiom `situation_model_reader._entity`'s `is_entity` / `reading_drive`'s `is_sentence_parse` already use), stamped on BOTH the belief/knowledge SmEntity and the desire SmEvent at mint time -- one rule covers both flavors.

microtheory.name: proposition_capture
microtheory.description: the ablatable eligibility flag for full-proposition (not head-grain) rendering of a modeled Level-2 belief/goal.

rules.name: mark_attitude_proposition_capture
rules.comment: A Level-2 belief/goal node (matched via its own `is_attitude_level2` self-edge) that carries a verbatim `proposition_span` and is not yet marked is flagged `proposition_capture=1` -- the DECISION that this node's full proposition (not just its head-grain `referent`/`idx_intentionality`) is eligible for rendering. Mint-once (the `Not(proposition_capture==1)` guard).
